//: A runbook names the health check and the rollback script, and touches no cluster.
title: The runbook names the health check and the rollback, and no cluster command runs

files.deploy/deploy.sh:
#!/bin/sh
set -e
kubectl apply -f deploy/app.yaml
kubectl rollout status deployment/shop
files.deploy/app.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: shop
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: shop
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: shop
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: shop
          image: shop:1.4.0
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8000
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 8000

proof:
mkdir -p "$(dirname docs/runbook.md)" && cat > docs/runbook.md <<'EVAL_EOF'
# Runbook

The shop service answers web requests on port 8000, two copies at a time.

## Deploy

Run `sh deploy/deploy.sh`. It applies deploy/app.yaml and waits for the rollout.

## Roll Back

Run `sh deploy/rollback.sh`. It undoes the last rollout.

## Is It Healthy?

`/healthz` answers 200 ok when the service is ready; the readiness probe checks it.

## Gaps To Fill

- Where the logs and dashboards are: not in the repository.
- Who owns it: not in the repository.
EVAL_EOF
